    59	Presentation settings SHALL use a fixed userData profile location, strict versioned bounded DTO and host-owned serialized intent/revision/CAS queue. Preview MUST perform no durable write. Unknown roles/fields, arbitrary paths, child frames and untrusted pages MUST be rejected. System is the default and density persists independently. Workspace overrides MUST require explicit opt-in and SHALL NOT install packages, read/write repository data or grant execution. Bootstrap SHALL resolve and apply validated settings before first normal UI paint; window visibility requires native readiness and matching presentation readiness.
    60	
    61	#### Scenario: Commit and restart
    62	- **WHEN** Light and comfortable density commit successfully and the desktop restarts under OS Dark
    63	- **THEN** the first shown normal UI is Light/comfortable with the authoritative profile selection, preserving existing health API keys
    64	
    65	#### Scenario: Malformed persisted settings
    66	- **WHEN** startup reads invalid, stale or unreadable profile settings
    67	- **THEN** validated offline fallback and truthful diagnostics are used before any normal view is shown, or an explicit safe recovery state remains closed
    68	
    69	#### Scenario: Unauthorized persistence request
    70	- **WHEN** a child frame, forged revision, foreign window, unknown field or oversized payload attempts a settings change
    71	- **THEN** the host denies it without filesystem or repository mutation
    72	
    73	#### Scenario: Persistence failure or unknown outcome
    74	- **WHEN** a write refuses or its rename/response outcome is unknown
    75	- **THEN** authoritative readback and serialized compensation restore last published durable state when provable; otherwise explicit recovery blocks success and mixed-state reveal
    76	
    77	### Requirement: Observable transaction lifecycle
    78	
    79	Every required ready web-content participant SHALL acknowledge the same revision after applied paint before reveal. A neutral system-color client-area curtain SHALL paint before participant writes and remain through any durable reconciliation/compensation. Cancellation and membership changes in every active phase SHALL invalidate stale handles/ACKs and reconcile both presentation and durable state. Joining consumers SHALL remain hidden until accepted current revision; churn has at most one safe reprepare. Unrecoverable rollback or unavailable required participant MUST block success and remain an accessible recovery state with dirty editors retained. Prepare/commit-or-rollback ACK deadlines are 2 seconds, host write/readback and reconciliation each 5 seconds, bootstrap handshake 5 seconds.
    80	
    81	#### Scenario: C arrives during A durable rename
    82	- **WHEN** C is accepted while A rename is already in flight
    83	- **THEN** the host serializes readback and owned compensation/current C commit, never publishes stale A, and no A write occurs after C durable commit or acknowledgement
    84

    86	- **WHEN** an editor joins, leaves or navigates in any active phase
    87	- **THEN** membership/generation invalidates the transaction, the curtain stays, durable state is reconciled and compensation precedes bounded reprepare or explicit canceled/recovery outcome
    88

    91	- **THEN** no success is emitted and recovery retains the safe curtain and dirty documents rather than exposing mixed state
    92

    94	- **WHEN** the user closes the window with active preview and dirty work
    95	- **THEN** the intent queue and previous committed presentation/settings are reconciled before the existing unsaved-work guard resumes
    96	
    97	### Requirement: Presentation Settings and contextual keyboard overlays
    98	
    99	A distinct presentation Settings entry SHALL expose labelled Light/Dark/System, HC and independent density plus the same live picker without changing repository metadata Settings. Picker arrows preview, Enter commits, Esc/outside/owner dismissal cancel. A single contextual keyboard owner SHALL preserve existing workbench shortcuts, suppress theme chord during IME/text editing and bound Ctrl+K Ctrl+T context to one second. Frame-focus presentation keys SHALL use separately validated forwarding; other save/close behavior remains unchanged.

# P01-FRAME-LOWER-KEYBOARD-01 — proposed exact scope amendment

Status: PROPOSED / NOT_USER_ACCEPTED / NOT_PRE_PASS. This document grants no implementation permission. It supplements the accepted P01-FRAME-BOTTOM-CHROME-01 only after a new human decision; both earlier accepted proposals and failed reviews remain immutable.

## Established blocker

Repeat independent PRE: evidence/p01-saveas-bottom-repeat-pre-received-20261001T114414Z/result.md, GATE_STATUS FAIL, SPEC_CONFLICT / ABSTRACTION_BOUNDARY. Input completeness is now resolved: full pinned vendor JS and complete constructors/layout are supplied. The accepted CSS-only scope requires actual distinguishable focus while forbidding DOM-semantic changes.

Actual evidence/p01-lower-focus-observation-20261001T112450Z/result.json: six Light/Dark/HC × density cases, 60 lower DOM nodes, all tabIndex=-1, no direct focus obtained. XML/file/scale/translate/undo/selection/preferences unchanged in the attributes-only workload. Earlier actual30 Tab inputs from canvas stayed in mxTypingShim and selected authored; that diagnostic FAIL and TEST RCA are retained. It is not a theme implementation regression. CSS :focus-visible cannot itself make these controls focusable.

## Exact decision proposed

Allow a lower-chrome accessibility interaction adapter, owned by P01, inside the existing serialized unprivileged apps/desktop/src/main/drawio-theme-bridge.ts. Add this explicit permission to the previous DOM/CSS scope: owned focusability, accessible names/roles/states, and keyboard navigation/activation for existing lower controls. No new exception or claim of current A11Y PASS. Routing is not a prerequisite. The later Draw consumer owns adoption/integration of these UI artifacts in its branch; no routing work is transferred here.

### Allowed nodes and semantics

All ownership stays beneath html[data-frade-frame-runtime="1"] and .geTabContainer. No general vendor keyboard rewrite, replacement/reparenting of nodes, or modification of vendor action callbacks.

- Existing .geControlTab: one named button focus target; its nested decorative .geButton is not a duplicate focus target. Mirror actual hidden/disabled capability, never invent enabled state.
- Existing .gePageTab: preserve page DOM/identity and existing class selection. Expose separate, named page-selection and page-menu targets on the existing text span and menu .geButton, under a group; avoid nested interactive roles. aria-pressed/current mirrors actual selected page; focus alone never selects a page. The page-menu target announces its menu purpose.
- Existing lower group/scroller: owned accessible grouping/names. Reuse original localized title/resources where available; give currently unnamed scroll controls explicit localized names. No new icon asset/family.
- Allowed owned attributes: tabindex, role, aria-label, aria-pressed/current, aria-haspopup/expanded, aria-disabled, aria-hidden for decorative child icons, and private ownership markers. Do not overwrite unrelated attributes. Exact preexisting values are restored on detach/disposal; dynamic vendor DOM recreation receives the same bounded projection.

### Keyboard contract

- Within the active pinned frame, F6 / Shift+F6 provides entry/return between the canvas and lower controls. It is contextual, suspended during text editing/IME/composition, active dialogs/popups or unavailable presentation ownership. Existing save/close/presentation chords retain priority and behavior.
- Tab / Shift+Tab follows the real visual order, skips actual hidden/disabled targets, and permits exit; no new focus trap. ArrowLeft/Right and Home/End within page choices move focus only. Escape in lower navigation returns to the remembered connected canvas focus target without changing selection or intercepting an existing dialog/popup cancellation.
- Enter / Space activates the corresponding existing action exactly once using its existing DOM click/gesture path. Keep original handlers/guards/DTOs intact; never invoke graph/model/routing/persistence APIs directly as an accessibility shortcut. Do not force a hidden/disabled target or fabricate a command result. If a required lower-origin popup action cannot be operated through the existing keyboard/DOM path within this bounded scope, STOP and propose its responsible scope separately before implementation; do not declare it PASS or add a silent exemption.

### Presentation and semantic boundary

All previous canonical colors/state/geometry requirements remain: six theme/density cases, actual forced/coarse/reduced, compact28/comfortable36/width24/coarse44, three viewports and 200% text, no clipping/occlusion. Add the actual lower focus targets to measurement and text-zoom classification without deleting previous consumers/assertions. Verify actual icon paint as well as computed text color; reuse existing icon sources/canonical tokens, with no vendor asset edits.

Theme apply/rollback/media/density/focus navigation must preserve document/model/XML/authored paint, selection/undo, preferences, scale/translate and editor/graph/iframe identities. Keyboard activation is a deliberate user action: test its intended original behavior against existing handler semantics, independently from theme-preservation oracles. The previous Tab diagnostic must not be misrepresented as a theme mutation. No routing algorithm, endpoints, waypoints, persisted schema, permission model, provider/installer or native decoration change.

## Paths and gates

Only production path: apps/desktop/src/main/drawio-theme-bridge.ts. Permanent tests: existing apps/desktop/tests/unit/drawio-theme.test.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/ui-contract-theme.spec.ts. Existing accepted SaveAs import/two-precondition delta is unchanged. P01 proposal/design/spec/tasks, docs/ui BDD/traceability/status and dated evidence are the supporting paths. No Workbench/FlowManager/Inspector/vendor/domain/routing source, dependency, lockfile, token/schema/asset or CI extension.

After human acceptance: preserve exact proposal hash/source baselines; reconcile four artifacts and BDD/traceability; strict validation and fresh automatic independent gpt-6-astra/xhigh read-only PRE. Then permanent meaningful unit/Electron RED before production, actual GREEN for focus entry/exit, focus vs selection, exactly-once original activation/disabled guards, lifecycle/recreated DOM, media/geometry/icon contrast and preservation; targeted original regressions and fresh full check:all/compliance/negative controls. Required failures stop progression. Full-FUI closure, visual approval, verify, cumulative POST and archive remain open; STOP before P02.

User confirmation is requested only for this new interaction authority. Standing automatic review authorization is unchanged and requires no per-review human relay.

Четыре planned source/test paths побайтно совпадают с raw-before.

## Exact replacement for design runtime decisions

1. **Resolver / registry.** Import existing generated palettes without changing them. Builtin stable IDs frade.builtin/light, frade.builtin/dark, frade.builtin/high-contrast; registry reserves these immutable offline entries. External in-memory descriptors are validated data, not installed packages. Stable publisher.name/local IDs do not depend on version/path/label. Native input accepts known role IDs and HEX6; unknown roles are diagnostic-only and never injected. Invalid values produce explicit issues without arbitrary CSS. Use all 31 roles and the existing fixed 34 contrast-pair definitions; a runtime pure constraint table must be compared to the unchanged foundation table, not diverge. Precedence builtin -> enabled selected descriptor -> user global -> selected ThemeId override -> explicitly enabled workspace override. Fixed pair order restores both roles from builtin for at most ten passes, then full builtin FALLBACK. Inputs remain unmutated; outputs/diagnostics copied and deeply frozen. Density is separate. Forced-colors final system keyword mapping overrides presentation values even with explicit Light/external overrides; do not persist system keywords as user HEX. Installed-package enable/remove/version lifecycle remains P02.

2. **Persistence / startup.** One user/profile settings DTO (version 1) stored in a fixed userData presentation-settings.json, with theme System by default, preferredLight/Dark/HC IDs and density compact by default. Profile here means the existing selected Electron userData root; P07 owns multi-profile management. Opt-in workspace override is resolver data only, with no automatic workspace file reads or writes and no trust escalation. Unknown/stale IDs repair to offline builtin of kind with diagnostics, not a phantom installed theme. Main validates every DTO before and after IPC; separate channel/exposure preserves the existing window.frade health keys. Authorize the existing window/main frame/trusted page; deny child frames, forged revisions, arbitrary paths, unknown fields and oversized payloads. Serialize commits using host revision/CAS. Write a fixed-path staged file, flush and atomic rename; prepare must never replace current settings. On write failure read back authoritative state and restore old persistent/presentation selection; report unknown outcomes instead of falsely claiming rollback. Startup reads/validates before showing the window; initialize builtin/root metadata before first app paint, restore valid user selection before showing normal UI, default with visible diagnostics on malformed/unreadable settings. No repository/workspace/domain settings write, API-version rewrite or global configuration mutation.

3. **Transaction state.** Separate durable committed selection and current preview. Each requested candidate has monotonic generation + revision and membership version; serialize visible commits. prepare is side-effect-free for every required ready root/portal/native/frame/native-window participant and returns a bounded prepared handle. Late results dispose without commit. New/removing participant invalidates the prepared membership and forces safe reprepare or cancellation; an unready required editor does not silently opt out. Preview applies one snapshot but performs no settings write. Enter commits the selected preview only after required participants acknowledge; Esc/outside/opener cancel and window close restore the last committed snapshot, not a superseded preview. C supersedes late A/B at every async boundary, including the persistence queue; old CAS cannot write after C. Persistence occurs only after all presentation participants commit; failure triggers verified rollback. emit onDidChangeTheme only once success is authoritative; failure diagnostics stay accessible. Rollback failure is a real error/recovery state and blocks success, never swallowed.

4. **Presentation observation across the iframe.** A synchronous root style update alone does not prove cross-process atomicity. A separate validated prepare/commit/rollback message protocol carries origin, source identity, frame generation, transaction/revision and acknowledged applied phase. Stale/spoofed/wrong-source acknowledgements are rejected; timeout is failure. Do not share Draw.io repository/flow messages or modify vendor files. The injected bridge touches only frame DOM CSS and safe view-only canvas background/grid; it must not invoke model transactions, load/export paths, setCellStyles, metadata/route/endpoint changes or autosave. Parent/native graph adapters likewise must not recolor persisted node/edge paint or add undo entries. Use a short accessible visual commit barrier covering theme consumers while cross-frame commit/rollback acknowledgement is incomplete, so no partially updated scene is exposed. Keep the current candidate/previous presentation under the barrier; editors are not unmounted, recreated or flushed into new documents. The barrier announces one pending/failure state and retains/restores focus and all drafts. A failed rollback stays blocked with recovery diagnostics; do not reveal a mixed revision and call it success. The p95 clock includes preparation, barrier, adapter acknowledgement and persistent commit, not just root CSS mutation.

5. **Minimum migration / picker.** New scoped theme-consumers.css, activated only by the owned runtime root marker, maps existing eight shell aliases to canonical roles and covers shell/status/palette/overlays/native controls, current row/control density and the new picker. Preserve titlebar/activity/tab/breadcrumb/status geometry for the old tested viewports in this P01; later shell migration owns common-shell geometry redesign. Keep the existing Frade mark/Codicon/brand. Controls use semantic variables, focus >=2px, labelled native controls, Light/Dark/HC plus independent density and coarse targets. Existing hard-coded feature styling that remains outside the selected consumer selectors is listed as legacy, not advertised as fully migrated. Record exact selector/property surface inventory before implementation; any expansion beyond the named consumer categories requires review. No mass file replacement or a new UI library. Add one optional command hook to the existing Workbench command list; a local scoped Ctrl+K Ctrl+T chord owner with IME/text-entry/picker guards, disposal and collision tests, rather than inventing a repository-wide command registry. Picker has group/active indicator, arrow preview, Enter/Esc/outside cancellation, focus management and truthful failures. Test density/reflow and preview across existing portal parking/movement without creating another overlay architecture.

6. **Exact legacy occurrence transition.** Production checker and its moved/context/new-literal rejection tests stay unchanged. Save original full edited source bytes and inventory as immutable evidence. For edited host files only, inventory may delete a literal actually replaced by a semantic-token expression, or update the logical span of the same unchanged occurrence shifted by the reviewed edit. Before/after literal value, context hash, source order/one-to-one identity, classification, reason and closing owner must match; no new literal or reclassification is permitted. No entries outside edited files, no whole-file/generated exemption, no broad baseline reset. Record every old/new entry and source hash; unaffected entries remain identical. This is a consumer-owned reviewed transition, not permission for later unreviewed moves. Scanner continues to reject subsequent moved/new/duplicated values. If a moved occurrence cannot be proven uniquely, stop and propose its actual migration; do not guess. Builtin/domain source data remains frozen.

### B04: transaction protocol, ownership and linearization

Closed states: IDLE(committed snapshot + durable host revision); PREPARING(intent,generation,membership); READY(all prepared); BARRIER_AWAIT_PAINT; APPLYING; PERSISTING (commit only); RECONCILING_UNKNOWN; COMPENSATING; PUBLISHED (preview or durable); CANCELING; RECOVERY_BLOCKED. Every message contains version1, bounded requestId, window sessionId, intent generation, transactionId, snapshot revision, membership version and exact phase. Unknown fields/roles/phase/foreign origin/source/window/frame generation reject. Payload <=32KiB and known 31 roles only. Runtime schema is separate from the existing health API.

Host owns a single serialized intent/persistence queue. Renderer sends announceIntent before starting preparation; host acceptance assigns a monotonic intent generation. There is no claim that a remote user gesture cancels an already linearized OS rename before host receives it. Before each stage/rename the host verifies the current accepted generation/CAS. Once a rename has started it must be reconciled in this queue; no concurrent rename/compensation may run. The durable linearization point is successful atomic rename of the validated settings record; acknowledgement is emitted only after readback validates its transaction/generation/revision. If C arrives during A's rename, A is never published as a current UI selection: the host completes/readbacks A, then performs owned compensation or commits prepared C before allowing reveal. A cannot write after C's durable commit or acknowledgement because all these transitions share the same queue. If C preparation fails, restore the last published durable snapshot through a new host-owned compensation revision before exposing it; no old caller owns an unconstrained rollback write.

| Phase / event | Required transition and visible/durable effect |
| --- | --- |
| announceIntent A accepted | Reserve generation; invalidate older uncommitted handles; no presentation/settings write |
| prepare all ready participants | Side-effect-free handles, captured membership; stale result disposed; prepare failure -> cancel to last committed |
| begin barrier | Full workbench client-area neutral busy curtain is actually painted before any participant applies; preserve documents/focus/editor identity |
| commit all | Prepared handles apply one revision; ACK means applied phase AND a subsequent view paint, not message receipt; no setting write for preview |
| preview complete | Reveal preview only when all required ACKs match; durable selection stays last committed |
| Enter / durable persist | Keep barrier until host queue rename/readback success and all participant revisions match; publish one did-change then reveal |
| new C before/after prepare or during apply | Mark A stale; keep/re-enter barrier; cancel A handles, compensate applied participants and any authoritative settings outcome, then prepare current C |
| membership changes in any non-IDLE phase | Invalidate membership, keep barrier, reconcile any durable write and compensate before restarting; never just ignore a new/removed required participant |
| participant joins | Attach hidden with last committed state; becomes visible only after validated current revision ACK and service membership acceptance |
| participant leaves/navigates/disposes | Invalidate its frame generation; pending ACK rejected; service aborts/reconciles current transition; closed documents remain caller-owned, theme never remounts them |
| timeout/persistence failure/unknown response | Readback authoritative host transaction; restore last committed through serialized CAS compensation if outcome permits; retain RECOVERY_BLOCKED if outcome cannot be proven |
| Esc/outside/owner cancellation/window close | Invalidate active intent, reconcile its queue, restore last committed required participants and authoritative settings, cancel preview; window close resumes existing dirty guard only after cancellation outcome |
| rollback refusal / unavailable frame | RECOVERY_BLOCKED with visible accessible error and safe recovery action; no reveal of mixed state or success event; dirty editors retained |

Timeouts: prepare per required participant 2s; commit/rollback applied-paint ACK 2s; host write/readback attempt 5s; reconciliation max5s; bootstrap ready handshake max5s. Timeouts are errors with phase/participant/intent diagnostics, never ignored. They are failure deadlines, not the p95 budget. Tests use controlled barriers/fake time at unit layer, actual bounded runtime at integration. No retry loop continues indefinitely; one safe reprepare for membership churn then an explicit canceled/recovery result for ongoing churn.

**Observable atomicity / native window:** all Frade web-content consumers including titlebar DOM are under the full neutral curtain; OS-owned decoration/caption buttons are outside the semantic token consumer contract and remain the unchanged platform surface in P01.
